issues.html:
🔗Matrix Live S13E15 - Website & Content Working Group updates

This episode, we're talking about the work of the Website & Content Working Group, and having a look behind the scenes in the production of This Week in Matrix itself. You can also read the news entry that is added during this video, down below!

Woah - a Matrix Live about This Week in Matrix, in This Week in Matrix... it feels like some kind of Inception scenario... 😎

🔗Dept of Status of Matrix 🌡️

🔗Governing Board (website)

The Governing Board is an advisory board to The Matrix.org Foundation and with elected representatives from all across the Matrix ecosystem.

HarHarLinks announces

Happy Friday, TWIM! It's been roundabout half a year since the last meeting and report from the Governing Board, though you might have been following this cycle's election process in May and June. I'm honored to follow in Greg's footsteps and announce the news this time as the Board's new chair, with a lot of support from our new vice-chair richvdh, and I am very grateful to Rich for taking the time to write up the report for you. 🙏 The Board gathered last week for its second meeting of the year for a comprehensive exchange of highlights in the Matrix world. As usual, you can find the comprehensive account in the blog post. We'd love to receive your feedback and questions - you can always find us at #governing-board-office:matrix.org.

If you'd like to learn more about how to get involved in the Foundation, the Governing Board, its members, structure, activities, Committees, Working Groups, or anything else, you can read a lot about this in the Foundation section right here on the matrix.org website. We're always excited about new ideas and initiatives - it's all of the ecosystem collaborating that really pushes Matrix forward.

Finally, in case you missed it until now, also watch the Foundation & Governing Board update from The Matrix Conference!

🔗Dept of Events and Talks 🗣️

🔗Stammtische (website)

HarHarLinks says

A Stammtisch ("regular's table") is a German meetup format where those with a shared interest meet regularly for discussion, exchange, and socialising.

Find more community organised events at matrix-community.events!

  • 19 November (3rd Thursday of every month) 19:00 CET: #matrix-stammtisch:freiburg.social at Blauer Fuchs. Learn more.
  • 19 November, 19:00 CET: #matrix-stammtisch:dresden.network at ro7. Learn more

Are you running a Matrix meetup? Add it to the list!

🔗FOSDEM 2027 (website)

Andy P says

FOSDEM will take place January 30-31, 2027 in Brussels.

A reminder that you have one more week to submit a proposal to the Decentralised Messaging Devroom! Check our blog post for the details. The deadline for submissions is 20 November.

More to come on FOSDEM very soon!

🔗Dept of Working Groups 💪

🔗Website & Content Working Group (website)

The Website and Content Working Group is responsible for the editorial and technical oversight of the main Matrix websites and social media channels.

MTRNord (they/them) reports

It has been 4 months since our last update and not only did we spend this time on lots of changes on the conference website but also we improved lots of other areas on the websites for you to enjoy!

🔗Overhauled Ecosystem Design

In the last update we already had major updates to the try-matrix page and also some improvements landed on the ecosystem pages. Since then we took this a step further and adapted the try-matrix design language also in the ecosystem. This means specifically for you:

  • A new Featured clients section matching try-matrix
  • Color coded pills 🌈
  • Better support for SPDX license definitions
  • Improved filtering (more colour!)
  • A better overview of available features in clients - if you spot a ❔ icon and know about that client supporting that feature, click the link on the bottom of the page to let us know!
  • Screenshots are back!
  • Big improvements to the bridges
    • Obsolete bridges are visually hidden
    • Clearer feature support
  • Better unified design across all ecosystem pages
  • Breadcrumbs to more easily navigate subpages

🔗Other Changes to matrix.org

Apart from the big ecosystem update there have also be plenty of other changes.

Many thanks to all contributors helping us keep the ecosystem data up to date, including @clins1994, @Mizerd, @dfuchss, @SpiritCroc, @bones-was-here, @wigmarbled, and @subpop! Thanks to you, our ecosystem directory keeps growing and existing entries stay accurate. ❤️

We've also been doing regular maintenance to keep the Foundation, Governing Board, and Working Group information fresh, including adding two new Working Groups and updating information about existing ones.

On the technical side, we've done some housekeeping, including cleaning up our metadata templates, ensuring our matrix.to links follow the specification, and updating our content contribution guidelines with more information on how we handle media on the website.

We also introduced a new policy for ecosystem listings: projects now need to have been active and supported Matrix for at least three months before being considered for inclusion. This should help us ensure that projects listed in the ecosystem are actively maintained and have demonstrated support for Matrix.

🔗A New Native Schedule System for the Conference Website

Another big change we did land in this timeframe has been the native schedule for The Matrix Conference website. This feature not only allowed us better visual integration into the conference page but also allows us to have new features which weren't possible before.

As a result we now have a new schedule which should be more accessible and bring more data sources together, we have the schedule also visible on the new live streaming page design (you'd have to catch it during the conference!) and last but not least we now have proper schedule widgets usable alongside the streams in rooms to support the remote conference experience.

🔗Other Changes to the Conference Website

Like with the matrix.org page here have been also a lot of smaller changes. Most prominently the team did an amazing job at ensuring the recordings were listed quickly as the conference ended, we overhauled both the livestream and the recordings page and we also improved our tooling around the recordings ingest to the page to reduce our turnaround times in the future.

🔗What Else Happened in the Working group?

Beyond the actual work on the websites, we also want to welcome xeni to the Working Group as our newest member who has joined us after helping us at The Matrix Conference 2026!

🔗If You Want to Contribute

If you want to contribute yourself to this feel free to check out both the website repository and the conference website repository or join us in our room at #matrix.org-website:matrix.org.

🔗Dept of Spec 📜

Andrew Morgan (anoa) {he/him} reports

Here's your weekly spec update! The heart of Matrix is the specification - and this is modified by Matrix Spec Change (MSC) proposals. Learn more about how the process works at https://spec.matrix.org/proposals.

🔗MSC Status

New MSCs:

  • MSC4581: Media annotations and universal alt text

MSCs in Final Comment Period:

  • MSC4492: Clarify that pagination tokens are directionless (merge)
  • MSC4388: Secure out-of-band channel for sign in with QR (merge)

Accepted MSCs:

  • No MSCs were accepted this week.

Closed MSCs:

  • No MSCs were closed/rejected this week.

🔗Spec Updates

The Spec Core Team have been laser-focused on Matrix 2.0 work post-conference. We're hoping to get the 2.0 release out in the next few weeks.

Of the... 37(!) total MSCs marked matrix-2.0 on the matrix-spec-proposals repo, there are 3 MSCs that have yet to be accepted and 9 MSCs which need a spec PR written.

Help is welcome, especially on the spec PR writing! A spec PR is the transformation from an MSC's free-form proposal text to the terse language of the Matrix spec (found in this repo).

On the MSC-acceptance side, MSC4576: Only allow data publishing when also allowing audio/video publishing on LiveKit transports is relatively uncontroversial, and likely just needs more eyes from the SCT.

The other two needs some more discussion, but they're close! Watch this space for the thrilling conclusion soon!

🔗Dept of Servers 🏢

🔗Zendrite (website)

pat-s reports

Zendrite, the Dendrite fork written in Go, released v3.9.0. This release brings faster remote room joins and a long list of newly supported MSCs.

Faster remote joins

  • MSC3902: Zendrite now implements the joining side of faster remote room joins, where a server joins with partial room state.
  • MSC3706: Zendrite also serves partial-state send_join responses to other servers.
  • Joins to rooms with a malformed allow list are refused instead of answering 500.
  • send_join and send_leave events are no longer echoed back to their sender.

Spec support

  • MSC4155 invite filtering.
  • MSC3881 remote toggling of push notifications, and MSC3890 removal of local notification settings when a device is deleted.
  • MSC4429 profile updates in /sync.
  • MSC2815, which gives moderators access to the content of redacted events.
  • MSC3874 relation type and MSC2326 label event filters.
  • MSC3930 poll and MSC4028 encrypted event push rules.
  • MSC4446 moving the fully read marker backwards, MSC4502 targeted room member queries and MSC4491 invite reasons in createRoom.
  • The room version org.matrix.msc3389.10 from MSC3389 is offered, and the unimplemented MSC4242 room version is no longer supported.

Sliding sync

  • Long polls no longer drain the database connection pool.
  • The legacy MSC3575 implementation is removed, which fixes missed list room updates.
  • Superseded requests stop quietly instead of logging foreign key violations.

Fixes

  • Identical state events sent by another user no longer bypass the auth rules.
  • m.room.member state events now go through the membership flows.
  • Unreachable remote profiles answer 502 and the failure is cached.

Release notes: https://codefloe.com/pat-s/zendrite/releases/tag/v3.9.0
Chat: #dendrite:matrix.org

🔗Synapse (website)

Synapse is a Matrix homeserver implementation developed by Element.

madlittlemods (Eric Eastwood) says

This week we have a new release, Synapse 1.165.0. To highlight:

  • We now have an initial, experimental implementation for efficient Server Announcements in Synapse. Server Announcements are for when an admin wants to message everyone on the server all at once (like announcing maintenance windows, policy changes, or incident notices), whereas the existing Service Notices are for admins to message people one by one (not efficient when you want to message everyone). There are still some rough edges that you can track in the epic, but it mostly just works for a client like Element Web.
  • The media download endpoints now skip reading from disk for HEAD requests so we can respond a lot quicker and avoid the unnecessary disk I/O (#20368, thanks to @JimKnoxx).
  • When using TLS listeners from Synapse itself, we now let the OpenSSL defaults shine through, which allows connections to negotiate the use of the post-quantum hybrid X25519MLKEM768 key-exchange group when supported by your OpenSSL version (#20374, thanks to @bardiharborow).
  • Synapse now prefers the notary response that stays valid longest rather than whichever arrived last. This helps when we receive responses from multiple notary servers which could previously cause event verification to fail (#20406, thanks to @AyeshaWaseemAhmad).

Thank you to all our contributors for helping to make Synapse the best it can be. As always, feel free to stop by #synapse:matrix.org to join in on the discussion, and if you encounter a bug, make sure to report it.

🔗Dept of Clients 📱

🔗Tesseract (website)

Marco says

Hello friends, this is the monthly-ish Tesseract update!

Now in version 0.9.8, several nice matrix goodies have been added:

  • Polls (creating, displaying, voting)
  • Display live location shares.
  • Message galleries (drag and drop more than one image/video/audio to the composer and they will be sent as a gallery)
  • Forwarded messages display a clickable link to the original (per MSC4553).
  • Display per-message profiles (per MSC4144).

Additionally, the login screen now has a 'find server' button that will show the user a list of available homeservers to pick from, fetched from https://joinmatrix.org.

On the UI side: configurable fonts, compact room list, pinned spaces sidebar, and timeline max width for wide screens.

Enjoy ;-)

🔗Sable (website)

F0rest reports

Hi TWIM! Sable here, just wanted to drop a quick note in here that we added support for MSC4495: Selective Presence, and we just released a blog post overview on how we are working on implementing Bundled URL Previews and adding new types of media to previews. Thanks!

🔗Robrix (website)

A high-performance, customizable client for power users. Its signature feature is a workspace layout with dockable tabs for chatting in many rooms and threads side by side. Written from scratch in Rust for all platforms.

Kevin Boos announces

Hi everyone, I'm happy to share the first ever TWIM update for Robrix, our Matrix client that has been in development for over 3 years (oof, didn't realize it had been so long). Robrix runs natively on all major platforms and is written from scratch entirely in Rust, and we do mean from scratch ... we also wrote the whole underlying UI toolkit (Makepad) and the platform abstractions framework (Robius) from scratch in Rust. This gives us unique control over every aspect of the app, including how it integrates with the underlying OS and how its UI behaves and adapts.

Robrix's goal is to be highly performant and efficient for power users, even under heavy use. Our signature "cool feature" is a multi-room dockable tabs layout (kinda like an IDE workspace), which lets you see and interact with as many rooms and threads as you want, all side-by-side. Each space gets its own dedicated layout too, so you can easily switch between custom room layouts on a per-space basis, instantaneously. We also have a neat multi-pane UI that lets you decide how extra room content is displayed, like pinned messages, threads, members list, room info, etc, even on mobile.

Robrix is also very intentional about letting you access any feature and any UI view on any device. So you can get the nice stacked mobile-like view on desktop, as well as the dockable workspace view on your phone or tablet. No limits! For example, you can zoom the UI to 112.8% if you want to, even on your iPhone.

I just got back from The Matrix Conference 2026 where I gave a talk about Robrix and some of our cool future directions, like custom generatable mini-apps that run right alongside your rooms or spaces, with a strict capability-like permissions model to ensure safety.

Since the conference, we've published two more beta releases, the latest one is available here. Some nice features we've added recently include:

  • 🛡️ Moderator tools to report, mute, kick, or ban users, plus a powerful tool to find, select, and delete spam messages
  • 🎨 Support for custom emoji and MXC URI media
  • 😀 Quick reactions, double-tap to react, and a super fast emoji picker and search popup
  • 🔍︎ Filter bubbles for the rooms list, like other clients but more flexible:
    • You can inverse/negate a filter (e.g., "non-low priority rooms") by long-pressing or middle/right-clidking it
    • We have more filters like "mod/admin rooms", and they can be combined in more ways
  • 🚪 When leaving a space, we show a nice hierarchical view for choosing which rooms/subspaces to leave
  • 📲 Tons of nice mobile-centric features: ↕️ auto-hide top & bottom bars when scrolling, and smoother/better virtual keyboard behavior
  • 🤏 Lots of effort to make the UI perfect and space-efficient on narrower screens & windows
  • 💬 Instantly discover and jump to old rooms (that have been tombstoned & replaced) with one tap
  • Android: ⚡ consistent 120Hz smooth refresh rate while animating, which 🔋 auto-reduces when idle to preserve battery
    • Plus support for 32-bit devices, Android 8+
  • ⚙️ Tons of new settings to customize lots of Robrix's UI appearance and behavior

Kindly give Robrix a try, and let us know what you think by joining our Matrix room here: #robius-robrix:matrix.org. I'm adding new features (and taking requests!) all the time.

🔗Nexus (website)

Matrix client made with Flutter and a Gomuks backend.

QuadRadical reports

Hello TWIM! This week, Nexus v1.1.0 is out, with many new features, quickly followed by v1.1.1!

You can grab it from the release page. If you use the Flatpak repo, the nightly builds, or the NixOS module, just update.

Here's what changed in 1.1.0:

  • Threads: You can now read and reply in message threads.
  • Polls: Create polls, vote in them, and end them.
  • Bot commands: Bots that advertise their commands using MSC4391 now get suggestions in the composer, along with a form for each command's options. Most of gomuks' built-in commands are supported too.
  • Room directory: Browse and join public rooms, and publish your own rooms to the directory.
  • Room upgrades: You can now upgrade a room to a newer room version, and rooms with a tombstone show a banner linking to the new room.
  • Account switcher: You can now be signed in to more than one account and switch between them.
  • Space improvements: You can now view a space's own timeline, and add or remove rooms from a space.
  • Custom emoji and stickers: Send emoji and stickers from image packs, and manage your packs in settings.
  • Reaction details: Hover over a reaction to see its shortcode, or open the new reactions popover to see who reacted with what.
  • Locations: Shared locations are now shown in the timeline.
  • Notification settings: Manage your push rules from inside Nexus, and set per-room notification levels from the room menu.
  • matrix: links: Nexus now opens matrix: URIs.
  • Event diffs: Changes to power levels, join rules, server ACLs, pinned messages and other room state now show exactly what changed.
  • Power level colours: Display names are now coloured by power level, with a setting to choose between per power level and per user colours.
  • Power level groups: Related permissions are now grouped in room settings, so you can set them all at once, or expand a group to set each one individually.
  • Weighted search: Emoji, user, room and settings search now put the best matches first.
  • Performance and fixes: Lower memory use, and fixes for read receipts.
  • And, as always, a whole lot of bug fixes 🙂

And in 1.1.1:

  • New media players: Nexus has switched from media_kit to new video and audio players. Videos also no longer autoplay on desktop.
  • Attachment previews: Attachments now show a preview in the composer before you send them.
  • Banned members warning: Before you view a room's banned members for the first time, Nexus warns you that they may have offensive names or avatars.
  • No more Play Services: The Android build was accidentally bundling Google Play Services through the location sharing library introduced in 1.1.0, thought it wasn't used at runtime. That's now fixed.
  • Fixes for crashes when loading audio messages on the Flatpak, and failed audio messages are now handled gracefully.

🔗What's next?

I'll keep fixing bugs as you find them, and keep working through the features that are still missing. If you run into anything, please let me know in #nexus:federated.nexus.

🔗Get involved!

If you want to help with development, report bugs, ask questions, or simply keep up with new features, join our Matrix room at #Nexus Client (https://matrix.to/#/!bdbbTYhctZTWzoTzn9:federated.nexus), or check out the Git repo at https://nexus.federated.nexus.

🔗Commet (website)

Commet is a client for mobile and desktop with a modern UI and fun features!

airyz reports

We recently released versions 0.5.1 and 0.5.2 of Commet!

v0.5.1 was mostly focused on some improvements to voice chat, we added an on screen overlay showing activity in your current call (supported on windows, x11 and wayland), and added support for system audio capture when screen sharing on Windows. it also contains a bunch of other small improvements, and is more optimized to use less resources in the background.

v0.5.2 contains an important security fix, so please be sure to update as soon as you can if you are a commet user!

https://github.com/commetchat/commet/releases/tag/v0.5.2

🔗Dept of VoIP 🤙

🔗LiveKit JWT service (website)

Bridging Matrix and LiveKit for Matrix RTC realtime sessions.

Johannes Marbach announces

lk-jwt-service 0.10.0 has been released and brings a bunch of important changes.

Most prominently, MSC4195 finally landed. 🎉 As a result, this release adds support for the stable Client-Server endpoints as per the merged version of the MSC. The unstable Client-Server endpoints and the legacy standalone endpoints remain supported in addition.

⚠️ IMPORTANT DEPRECATION NOTICES: Serving the Client-Server endpoints as per the MSC requires setting up lk-jwt-service as an application service on the homeserver. Since the MSC has been accepted, not running as an application service is deprecated as of this release and support for it will be removed in future versions. Details on how to configure the application service can be found in README.md. For the same reason, fronting more than one homeserver via LIVEKIT_FULL_ACCESS_HOMESERVERS is deprecated as well and will be removed in future versions. This setting already only affects the legacy endpoints. For security reasons it is strongly recommended to only put the one homeserver that lk-jwt-service was set up as an application service for into LIVEKIT_FULL_ACCESS_HOMESERVERS.

A last-minute change in the MSC was to RECOMMEND granting publishing permissions to remote users. This acts as a fallback and allows users to join sessions even if their own homeserver doesn't provide an SFU. Server operators can granularly control whether to allow remote publishing with the new LIVEKIT_REMOTE_CAN_PUBLISH_HOMESERVERS environment variable.

A related change in the final MSC was to RECOMMEND disabling the permission to update one's own metadata for participants. The service now disables this permission by default on tokens. Admins that rely on this feature, may reenable the permission with the new LIVEKIT_CAN_UPDATE_OWN_METADATA environment variable.

MSC4196 also landed and to support the transition to its stable identifiers, the service now maps m.call#ROOM slot IDs to m.call#room. This means clients will end up in the same LiveKit room regardless of which spelling they used.

Finally, lk-jwt-service is now able to bind to a Unix socket via the LIVEKIT_JWT_BIND environment variable. Thanks to GitHub user @cyberb for contributing this feature.

🔗Dept of Ops 🛠

🔗Connectivity Tester

MTRNord (they/them) announces

A homeserver report now covers more than basic federation reachability, so there are more choices about what to run and more detail to make sense of afterwards. Here are a few highlights from the latest release.

🔗Pick the Checks You Need

The homepage has a "What to check" picker. Outgoing federation, Client API / Matrix 2.0, MatrixRTC / Element Call, and Neoboard can be selected separately. The result then shows tabs for the categories you chose, instead of making you scroll through checks you did not run. Alerts and probe jobs also have federation-only, standard, and extended presets.

Some checks are useful when you need a closer look:

  • The room-version check reports which Matrix room versions a homeserver accepts. It sends a signed synthetic federation invite for each version, so the picker labels it as making extra requests.
  • The experimental MSC4496 calendar check looks for the client and federation availability endpoints. It only checks whether those routes exist; it does not request calendar data.
  • The MatrixRTC results show whether the server advertises sticky events (MSC4354), which Neoboard's LiveKit mode and Element Call's Matrix 2.0 mode need.

🔗Read Connectivity Results More Easily

The results page opens with a health summary. When you scroll down, a slim bar keeps the server name and the main results in view. Section headers show useful status without opening them, and the connectivity section starts with the number of working addresses, TLS versions, and whether ECH is enabled.

Certificates are grouped instead of repeated for every IP, while each address has its own collapsible details. When a server advertises Encrypted Client Hello, the tester also verifies the public-name certificate a client sees if its ECH attempt is rejected. The report for mtrnord.blog shows that certificate alongside the regular one.

🔗Alerts for Unsteady Connections and ECH

Alerts now confirm an outage from a window of recent checks: three failures in the last five checks by default. A single successful check during an unreliable spell therefore does not reset the whole confirmation. If a server keeps flipping between down and recovered, its status and history still update, but down/recovered emails and webhooks are suppressed while it is flapping. The recent checks and transitions are saved with the alert, so a restart does not reset that decision. The alerts overview also shows down and recovered changes live.

Outgoing federation checks also need strong evidence before they treat an address family as unsupported. Even when that result is cached, a background probe keeps checking for recovery. Alerts that have stayed down for more than a week are checked hourly, so recovery is still noticed without running a full check every minute.

ECH is covered by alert notifications too. For alerts with TLS expiry warnings enabled, the sooner expiring of the regular and ECH public-name certificates sets the warning date. If the ECH certificate expires first, the email and webhook name its public name. A replaced ECH certificate can also trigger the TLS certificate-change notification when that option is enabled.

🔗Share a Report

The actions are together in one place: get a permalink, re-run the check, or open the Export menu. Markdown now follows the report's sections, including the overview, problems, and individual checks. The redesigned PDF has a light theme for printing and a dark theme for screens, with a verdict banner and compact stat cards.

Try it at https://connectivity-tester.mtrnord.blog/. The changelog, source code, and support forum have more details and a place for feedback.

issues.html:
🔗Matrix Live - Foundation & Governing Board Update

🔗Dept of Status of Matrix 🌡️

🔗Governing Board (website)

The Governing Board is an advisory board to The Matrix.org Foundation, with elected representatives from all across the Matrix ecosystem.

🔗Governing Board meeting, Nov 2026

HarHarLinks says

Hi all, it's been half a year since the Governing Board's last report which means this week it was time for us to gather for the second Board meeting of the year!

We're busy getting a proper report ready to share with all of you, so this is just a teaser, but I hope we will be able to include it properly in the next TWIM!

As a tiny teaser, we thank Max who joined the Board as a representative for the Individual Members of the Foundation only during the last election cycle, but unfortunately had to leave the Board again long before the end of his term due to life happening. 🙏 Instead we're excited to announce that we're joined by Reid Anderson, the runner-up Individual Member candidate from the elections earlier this year! 🎉

You can find the info about the Board, its Committees and all members at https://matrix.org/foundation/governing-board/.

🔗Dept of Events and Talks 🗣️

🔗The Matrix Conference

Andy P announces

We're happy to wrap up The Matrix Conference 2026 by sharing the official event photos with you! Please note the information provided in the README.txt file.

All talks from the Conference were recorded and are available for streaming on demand through our archive page including downloadable slides. If you're a speaker of a recorded talk and your slides are missing, please send them to us at conference@foundation.matrix.org so we may make them available.

We are currently looking at some great options for venues in The Netherlands for The Matrix Conference 2027. If you know of a venue we should definitely check out, please share it with us via email to conference@foundation.matrix.org.

🔗FOSDEM

Andy P reports

The next major event on The Matrix.org Foundation radar is FOSDEM 2027 which will be happening on January 30-31 in Brussels, Belgium 🇧🇪

The Call for Proposals for the Decentralised Messaging Devroom is open now, and runs until Friday November 20th. We'd love to see your submissions for Matrix-related talks.

Watch this space for news about other Matrix-related content and happenings around FOSDEM!

🔗Stammtische (website)

HarHarLinks says

A Stammtisch ("regular's table") is a German meetup format where those with a shared interest meet regularly for discussion, exchange, and socialising.

Find more community organised events at matrix-community.events!

  • 9 November (2nd Monday of every month) 20:00 CET: #matrix-stammtisch:ccc.ac at CCCAC. This month we're excited to celebrate its first anniversary! 🎉
  • 11 November (2nd Wednesday of every Month) 19:00 CET: #matrix-stammtisch:koeln.ccc.de at C4

Are you running a Matrix meetup? Add it to the list!

🔗Widgets Working Group

Timo K. says

The Working Group has formed, and the first meetings have been held.

Outcomes so far:

  • Organisational foundations: Sponsor, Chair, Website, Rooms.
  • There is a bi-weekly Widget Clinic (a meeting in which technical topics are discussed: the spec, SDKs, bouncing ideas off each other about widget solutions). The goal is to get the ecosystem, and specific solutions, into a healthy state.
  • We are making progress on an overview of how Matrix can be extended. Several conversations ended up on what we truly need in the ecosystem. The conclusions will be are presented soon here. This is fundamental to justifying the current MSCs, because it answers the question: Why the proposed solution should end up in the spec.

Join our room if you want to help out: #widgets-working-group:matrix.org

🔗Dept of Spec 📜

Andrew Morgan (anoa) {he/him} says

Here's your weekly spec update! The heart of Matrix is the specification - and this is modified by Matrix Spec Change (MSC) proposals. Learn more about how the process works at https://spec.matrix.org/proposals.

🔗MSC Status

New MSCs:

  • MSC4578: Cross-client Shared Search Indexes of encrypted messages
  • MSC4577: Soundboards for MatrixRTC calls
  • MSC4576: Only allow data publishing when also allowing audio/video publishing on LiveKit transports
  • MSC4575: MatrixRTC m.full_mesh transport
  • MSC4574: linked state events
  • MSC4573: Atomically increasing versioned account data

MSCs in Final Comment Period:

  • No MSCs are in FCP.

Accepted MSCs:

  • No MSCs were accepted this week.

Closed MSCs:

  • No MSCs were closed/rejected this week.

🔗Spec Updates

Lots of new and fun MSCs have been put up this week! Feel free to have a look through the above.

After the dust from The Matrix Conference has settled, the Spec Core Team have been trying to wrangle the remaining two, err three, Matrix 2.0 MSCs.

This week MSC4576 sprung up under the Matrix 2.0 label. It's a tiny follow-up to MSC4195: LiveKit transport for MatrixRTC to enable applications other than VoIP to use MatrixRTC channels (such as Neoboard). It's non-controversial, so expect it to be accepted by the SCT fairly rapidly.

Otherwise, the SCT is focusing on wrapping up the Matrix 2.0 saga, getting it out, and then moving on to the backlog of other MSCs waiting in the queue. Thank you for your patience, and feel free to review and comment on and refine the landscape of MSCs in the meantime!

🔗Dept of Servers 🏢

🔗Arminius (website)

Arminius is a new enterprise homeserver in development.

Nico says

Heya, Nico here, with my corporate hat on!

For the last almost 2 years my team at Famedly have been secretly working with the BWI on a new homeserver for them. Now we finally published the repository for it and will continue working in the open from now on.

However, the homeserver is not done yet. So please do not actually use it yet. We want to first make sure it behaves as a proper citizen of the federation and we still have a few complement tests to pass as well as do a proper audit and fixup some of the corners we have cut at the start of development.

You might be wondering why one would want to write a new homeserver. We gave one explanation at The Matrix Conference and thanks to the amazing video and conference team as well as all the volunteers, you can actually watch the recording here: https://conference.matrix.org/watch/#why-is-there-rust-in-our-matrix

If you are not much of a video fan, the brief gist of it is:

  • We want a scalable homeserver, that we can run in a high-availability setup without any single process of failure. (That's what SPOF stands for, right?)
  • We want the server to be reliable, because surprises are for people, not computers!
  • And we want it to have all the enterprise-y fun bits like easy to deploy on k8s and integrate with all the enterprise tools the BWI likes or rather gets to deal with.

Long term this will also be our base for our MLS work.

So far it has been pretty fun developing a homeserver while trying to follow the spec and please do expect a few spec clarification PRs as well as contributions from complement from us. You don't often get to see the spec from that lens and I hope we can leave the spec in a better place for the next 20 homeservers!

If anything here sounded interesting, do check out our repo, but don't look too closely, it is always a bit embarrassing to present something you have built!

As an aside, we also built our own test suite and have been trying it out on Continuwuity, which has been quite interesting. It is a lot of fun to work with others in the ecosystem!

We also plan to make an MSC out of our homeserver migration format once we gathered some experience with it, which will surely make development of other homeservers more interesting to people, who already have a homeserver deployed.

That is all I have for you this time. You likely will have to wait for the next update for a while, but we do intend to share when Arminius becomes usable and you can try it out. In the meantime you can always find us on Matrix!

🔗Zendrite (website)

pat-s announces

Zendrite, the Dendrite fork written in Go, released v3.7.0. This release catches up with Matrix spec v1.16 to v1.19, adds two moderation features and repairs rooms whose stored state went wrong.

Spec support

  • /versions now advertises Matrix v1.16 through v1.19.
  • MSC4108 QR code login, which lets a new device sign in by scanning a code from a device that is already logged in, using the rendezvous from MSC4388.
  • MSC4306 thread subscriptions, so users can follow individual threads.
  • MSC4262, which delivers profile updates over sliding sync.
  • The Matrix v1.17 changes MSC4190, MSC4210 and MSC4326.

Moderation

  • MSC4284 policy servers, which a room can use to screen events before they are accepted.
  • MSC4380 invite blocking, which lets users block unwanted invites.

Room state repair

  • The roomserver repairs state events that were stored under the wrong state key, and skips rejected outliers while doing so.
  • Events that were rejected are rechecked against the repaired state, redactions together with the events they redact, and events together with the rejoin that follows their cited join.
  • Messages that were rejected along with their sender's membership are accepted.
  • Memberships the local repair cannot settle are taken from other servers, and outlier memberships that follow the current state are added.
  • Forked memberships are passed on even when a room has nothing else to add, and the memberships other servers hold for users the repair leaves alone are logged.

Release notes: https://codefloe.com/pat-s/zendrite/releases/tag/v3.7.0
Chat: #dendrite:matrix.org

🔗Dept of Bridges 🌉

🔗slack2matrix

Adam reports

slack2matrix is a one-shot Slack workspace importer that fills in several gaps from prior solutions, including by providing full migration of media/attachments. It imports your Slack export into Matrix as an end-to-end encrypted space. Each Slack channel becomes an encrypted room inside the space. Every Slack user can be mapped to a Matrix user and optionally cross-signed with that Matrix user’s recovery key. Every message, thread, reaction, and file is imported with its original author and timestamp, and all media is encrypted on the client before upload, so the homeserver never stores a plaintext copy of the history. Hyperlinks between messages in different Slack channels are translated to Matrix room hyperlinks.

Try it out: https://github.com/matrix-axon/slack2matrix

🔗Dept of Clients 📱

🔗Sable Chat (website)

F0rest says

Hi TWIM! We haven't talked since we released v2.0.0, and as we're now on [checks notes] v2.3.5(!) there's quite a bit to catch up on. Firstly: we're on the Apple App Store! Yes, it's taken this long to get on the App Store. It happens. We're also on Google Play Store now, so users don't have to download APKs anymore. Here's three weeks of new features:

In calls, we now have push-to-talk and other global call shortcuts on Desktop. We now have screensharing with audio everywhere, thanks to our Electron migration, which has also allowed us to support Wayland. You can also now configure if you want to use hardware encoding and/or decoding.

In accessibility, we have more comprehensive keyboard navigation, screen readers announce new messages, and better screen reader support during setup and sign-in. (We're always striving for better accessibility -- if you have access needs, or experience doing accessibility audits, please reach out!)

In user experience, so much! We have amazing hand-crafted UI sounds & ringtone (thanks Mae), a nice inline audio player, color-scheme sync on Linux desktop, tons of new customisation like overriding fonts. We now have a lovely notification tray instead of an annoying banner when the app tries to self-update. We have a nice landing page for when you first open the app, instead of just dumping you on a blank screen. We're always iterating on UX, and with 4510 new commits there's a lot we can't quite outline.

Some other stuff: in notifications, we have more granular notification rules, and we now prevent notifications reaching other devices if you're currently using Sable. We now have tray support everywhere, you can edit captions on messages, sensitive data is stored on the system keyring, DeArrow support for YouTube embeds, and a Nix flake for building your own desktop builds. We now ship a hosted option, similar in architecture to Gomuks, and Sable can now register as a handler for matrix: URIs.

Phew! That's about three weeks of changes. It's been a very very busy time for us at Sable, as we grow from a solo fork of Cinny to a fully fledged, independent and hopefully-maturing codebase. I'd like to thank Erwan for tirelessly working on Sable every day, handling scary business things like DUNS and App Store Connect, going above and beyond in delivering the best for not only us but upstreaming changes to Matrix Rust SDK and quickly familiarising with Continuwuity to push our ecosystem forward. We've started getting contributor cross-over with Continuwuity (thanks Ginger!) and it makes me excited to see what we could do if we start reaching out to other projects.

If you're part of the ecosystem, whether it's a bridge bot, homeserver, or other integration, please reach out! We have a simple mission of creating the best Matrix client out there -- not just a Discord clone, not just a JSON debugger, but something truly Matrix we can give to users: with great UI, UX, accessibility, leading feature support, and no vibecoding!

Sable is a Matrix client, available on iOS, Android, Web, and Desktop Platforms. You can view our Git repo, and join our Matrix space at #sable:sable.moe. 🏳️‍⚧️

🔗Extera (website)

rustyraven[extera] says

Hi! Extera now supports more languages than ever before. New languages include Finnish, Polish, Ukrainian, and Turkish. Minor improvements: the new group page is now used for creating chats in spaces (meaning you can manually toggle E2EE and visibility options), and a fix for forwarding gallery messages.

That's all what was changed in Extera, have a nice day!

Website ・ Try Extera ・ Releases ・ Source code ・ Matrix space

🔗ytalk-ng (website)

dirk says

Hi everyone! I’d like to introduce ytalk-ng, a native Matrix client for iPhone, iPad and Mac, inspired by irssi and the classic Unix chat tool ytalk. It’s currently available in beta through TestFlight, and I’m looking for people to try it out and share their feedback.

If numbered chat windows, slash commands and an activity indicator like [Act: 2,3,5!] feel like home, this might be for you. ytalk-ng brings that style to Matrix with a green-on-dark terminal look, monospace text and keyboard shortcuts. There’s also a ytalk-inspired split-screen view for conversations.

Underneath the retro interface, it supports encrypted rooms and direct messages, device verification and key backup. You can use an existing account on a homeserver that supports Simplified Sliding Sync, signing in with OAuth or a password.

This is still a beta, so please expect bugs and rough edges. I’d especially appreciate feedback on everyday usability, homeserver compatibility and how the interface feels on different devices. Bug reports and ideas are very welcome!

Join the beta on TestFlight

Website and screenshots · Support and feedback

🔗Element X iOS (website)

A total rewrite of Element iOS using the Matrix Rust SDK underneath and targeting devices running iOS 17+.

Doug announces

The 26.11.0 release candidate is out and should reach the App Store on Monday. Its headline changes are:

  • Reply with a voice message. You can now reply to any message with a voice recording.
  • Custom image reactions. Reactions that use an image now render in the timeline, animated GIFs included!
  • Right-to-left text. Mixed LTR and RTL text is now properly aligned within the message bubble.

Also in this release: members of an allowed space can join knock_restricted rooms directly, we fixed a bug when opening notifications that belong to a thread and the message search tab explains its three-month history limit. Element Call moves to its final 0.28.2 release.

Outside of the release, our work on Multi-Account support continues, with each signed-in account getting its own service for Notifications, Calls & Location Sharing and we’re getting everything ready to allow presentation of the add-account flow.

Andy P announces

ADMIN magazine has a lengthy article this week about running your own Matrix Server (specifically using Synapse). https://www.admin-it.io/running-your-own-matrix-server-with-synapse/

issues.title: This Week in Matrix 2026-10-30
issues.html:
🔗Matrix Live - The Matrix State of the Union

🔗Dept of Events and Talks 🗣️

Andy P says

We've wrapped up The Matrix Conference for this year!

We've dedicated this week's Matrix Live slot to bring you The Matrix State of the Union from the event, in case you missed it. We've also just posted a full write-up of highlights, including links to many of the talks, all of which are available to watch online right now.

Next on our radar: FOSDEM 2027! Planning is well underway, and we're happy to share the Call for Participation in the Decentralised Messaging Devroom. If your talk did not make it onto the schedule for The Matrix Conference, why not consider submitting it for FOSDEM? We'll have more information to share about our broader plans for FOSDEM over the next few weeks.

🔗Matrix in the News 📰

Andy P announces

Happy to see several news reports that came out of The Matrix Conference last week.

  • The Register covers digital sovereignty, and the need for greater funding.
  • ComputerWorld also talks about the overall European public sector movement.
  • Computer Weekly focuses on Luxembourg and Austria case studies.

🔗Dept of Spec 📜

Andrew Morgan (anoa) {he/him} announces

Here's your weekly spec update! The heart of Matrix is the specification - and this is modified by Matrix Spec Change (MSC) proposals. Learn more about how the process works at https://spec.matrix.org/proposals.

🔗MSC Status

New MSCs:

  • MSC4569: Calendar
  • MSC4568: DTMF for MatrixRTC

MSCs in Final Comment Period:

  • No MSCs are in FCP.

Accepted MSCs:

  • MSC4551: Sliding Sync Extensions: Receipts
  • MSC4548: Sliding Sync Extensions: Account data
  • MSC4543: Sliding Sync Extensions: End-to-end encryption
  • MSC4538: Sliding Sync Extensions: To-Device messages
  • MSC4354: Sticky Events
  • MSC4196: Voice and video calling application for MatrixRTC
  • MSC4195: LiveKit transport for MatrixRTC
  • MSC4143: MatrixRTC – Real-time communication over Matrix

Closed MSCs:

  • No MSCs were closed/rejected this week.

🔗Spec Updates

Hello from The Matrix Conference hackathon!

We have a blur of MSCs being accepted this week! All of them are related to the big push last week to get Matrix 2.0 MSCs over the line. Sans MSC4480 and MSC4075, they have all now landed! 🎉

Once the SCT has had some days to recover from the conference, they will work to get these remaining MSCs in shape for merging. After that, Matrix 2.0 will shortly follow!

Matrix conference talks related to Matrix 2.0 MSCs:

  • Bringing MatrixRTC to the Matrix Ecosystem
  • Matrix State of the Union

Outside of Matrix 2.0, the new MSC4569 federated calendaring MSC is also off the back of a Matrix conference talk this week. Give it a watch!

🔗Dept of Trust & Safety ⚖️

🔗policyserv (website)

A proactive safety and moderation tool for Matrix communities.

TravisR reports

PolicyServ v1.8.0 has been released! Aside from the plethora of dependency updates, this release primarily contains a refactor to use MSC4456 harms taxonomy internally. By using the harms taxonomy, we're able to more clearly communicate why an event wasn't allowed in a room via MSC4387's M_SAFETY error code (when client support follows).

The refactor may have changed how some filters behave or work. We encourage using a staging environment where possible, though it's safe to roll back to v1.7.0 if something goes wrong. Let us know if you run into any bugs in #policyserv:matrix.org.

The Foundation's policyserv instance is available to communities, and has been running the release over the weekend.

🔗Dept of Servers 🏢

🔗Synapse (website)

Synapse is a Matrix homeserver implementation developed by Element.

madlittlemods (Eric Eastwood) says

This week we have a new release, Synapse 1.164.1. To highlight:

  • We've been busy this week addressing the onslaught of security advisories reported in our dependencies. This required a few patch releases to bump pillow used for media, msgpack to fix a memory exhaustion issue reachable through the public room list API, and certifi/rustls-webpki to distrust the compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates. As with any security issue, it's recommended to update as soon as you can!
  • Synapse now advertises support for Matrix v1.16 and v1.17 (#20333, #20334).
  • The experimental MSC4140 Delayed Events and MSC4354 Sticky Events implementations had a flurry of updates, as the spec solidified in time for the Matrix Conference.
  • Media uploads no longer leave behind orphaned files on disk when they exceed the media_upload_limits (#20006).
  • A couple more Synapse Rustification updates including laying the foundation for a Rust-backed database pool (#19996) and a clock source on the Rust side (#20294).

Thank you to all our contributors for helping to make Synapse the best it can be. As always, feel free to stop by #synapse:matrix.org to join in on the discussion, and if you encounter a bug, make sure to report it.

🔗Dept of Bridges 🌉

🔗Bolt / Lightning

jersey reports

After about two weeks of work or so, Bolt and Lightning v0.9.7 are out!

I've almost entirely rewritten Matrix support from scratch without relying on an external library, and it now properly handles sending/receiving custom stickers and emoji, lets you use just per-message-profiles to bridge if you've previously used an appservice, should work a lot better on non-Synapse homeservers, and also features a lot of fixes for other platforms too.

Lightning is an open-source bridge bot and bot framework I've been working on for about four years which supports Discord, Spacebar, Harmony, Fluxer, Stoat, Telegram, Matrix, IRC (including IRCv3 magic), Osmium, Matterbridge's API, and its own REST API, in addition to Matrix. Bolt is the free hosted version I offer that supports the platforms above, with Libera.chat and OFTC being the two currently supported IRC networks.

You can find more in the changelog, lightning website, bolt website, codeberg repo, or in https://matrix.to/#/#bolt:ineedmore.money and https://matrix.to/#/#lightning:ineedmore.money

🔗Dept of Clients 📱

🔗iamb (website)

A terminal-based Matrix client that uses Vim keybindings.

ulyssa announces

iamb v0.0.13 was released earlier this week! :tada:

This release includes:

  • Support for rendering polls, listing pinned events, and a :message command to view extra message details.
  • Improvements to the room lists to show unread counters, section headers for grouping rooms together, and support for customizing which labels are shown next to rooms
  • Support for viewing unjoined rooms in spaces and viewing room previews before joining.
  • Support for custom theming, ~60 themes that have been ported from Vim, and options for expanding the username color palette.
  • Support for OAuth login
  • New :ignore and :self invites set block commands for dealing with spam and abuse.

See the v0.0.13 releases page for downloads and the full changelog, and the website or manual pages for updated docs and theme details.

🔗tacit (website)

Dominik [m] reports

Back in April I introduced Tacit here, my desktop-first Matrix client and fork of Tammy. Since then it has grown from "works on my machine" into something you can actually download: the first releases are out 🎉 The current one is 26.9.2-tacit.7.

You can grab builds for macOS (Apple Silicon), Windows and Linux, and the web version is available as a Docker image (ghcr.io/dfuchss/tacit). If you just want to try it without installing anything, there is a public web instance at https://tacit.fuchss.org. The version number tells you which Tammy release it is based on, so Tacit keeps following upstream and picks up new Tammy and trixnity-messenger features over time.

🔗What's new since the first announcement

  • Guilds got categories: spaces are still shown as guilds, but you can now group rooms into categories (subspaces), browse them and invite people to a whole guild or category
  • A calmer timeline: messages from the same sender are grouped, mentions get a soft highlight, and failed messages can be retried right where they are. New in 26.9.2-tacit.4: runs of room events (joins, invites, room settings, …) collapse into a single row like "6 room events by Alice and Bob" that expands on click, so a fresh chat no longer starts with a wall of notices
  • Nicer replies: quotes are now a card in the quoted person's colour with their avatar and name, clicking one jumps to the original message and briefly highlights it, and the composer shows who you are replying to
  • Small things I use every day: room filters, mark as read/unread, first slash commands (e.g. /spoiler), reactions that show who reacted, a system font option, and a native unread badge in the macOS Dock (whose icon now finally has the same size as its neighbours)
  • Updates itself: the desktop app checks for new releases about once a day, verifies the download and installs it when you click Restart to update. You can turn this off under Settings › About the app. Starting with 26.9.2-tacit.3, you only have to install Tacit by hand once

Tacit is still alpha and still a weekend project for friends and me, so expect rough edges. The builds are not signed yet; the README explains how to start them anyway.

  • Download & source: https://gitlab.com/dfuchss/tacit
  • Project page: https://fuchss.org/projects/tacit/
  • Feedback and issues are welcome on GitLab

🔗Extera (website)

rustyraven[extera] announces

Hi federation! We've made several changes to Extera since our latest TWIM post.

🔗Improved call UX

We've added call controls above the navigation bar, so you can quickly mute/unmute the microphone, go back to the call page and hang up. On the call page, you can now pin the participant view and choose which screen share to watch.

🔗Media galleries

Experimental support for MSC4274 media galleries! Rendering is always enabled, but sending them requires Settings → Chat → Use experimental galleries.

🔗Improved message forwarding

MSC4553 is now supported, with plaintext and HTML fallback.

🔗Location warning

Tapping "Send location" in a large (≥50 members) or public room now shows a warning first. We've actually seen people send their location to public rooms.

🔗Improved update checker

It now uses Extera's Forgejo instance and shows the changelog directly in the update notification.

🔗Custom chat tags

Assign custom tags to chats ー they will show up at the top of the chat list, like chat folders in Telegram.

🔗Extera on the web

Try it out: https://app.extera.xyz/

Website ・ Try Extera ・ Releases ・ Source code ・ Matrix space

🔗theGrid (website)

Victor Tran announces

It's been a while, but I've released v0.2 of theGrid this week. This release of theGrid introduces the following changes:

  • You are now required to verify your session to use theGrid.
  • Multi-SFU support is now available for calls
  • Per-user volume controls are now available in a call
  • You can now change your profile picture in your Account Settings

You can grab it from the website: https://thegrid.vicr123.com/ Or join the space to chat: #theGrid:bnbdiscord.net

n.b. theGrid v0.2.1 was released shortly after, containing a security update that disables some known bad TLS certificates. If you are using theGrid, it is recommended to update to theGrid v0.2.1 as soon as possible.

🔗Mactrix (website)

Viktor Strate announces

The latest release of Mactrix (a native macOS Matrix client) contains a lot of new features that I have been working on over the last month's time. Here are the highlights:

  • Rewrite entire timeline in AppKit The timeline view has been rewritten purely in AppKit without any SwiftUI components. This simplifies things compared to the previous hybrid implementation that required a lot of fragile bridging code. This means that the new timeline is more capable, way faster, and more stable. For instance, the timeline now groups consecutive messages from the same sender and collapses consecutive status updates.
  • Attachment uploading Attachments can now be added to messages by dragging or pasting files or media to the message composer. You can add several attachments to the same message. The attachments are sent together with the message text.
  • Sidebar space grouping Rooms and sub-spaces are now grouped into your top level spaces.
  • Mentions User mentions in messages now show as a visual colored pill with their avatar image next to it. You can now also mention users by writing an @ symbol to open an autocomplete popup with all users in the room.
  • Message editing Messages can now be edited directly in the the timeline, by pressing the new pencil icon from the action bar when hovering over the message.
  • Better link handling in messages When clicking https://matrix.to links, the app will now load the link directly inside the app instead of opening the web browser. Usernames in status messages can now also be clicked to open details about their profile.
  • User drag and drop The initial work for supporting general drag and drop has been implemented for users. You can now drag users from the timeline or the inspector. Currently, you can only drop them into the message composer to mention them, but in the future this could be extended to invite users to rooms or change their permissions.

If the project sounds interesting, come say hi in our room #mactrix:qpqp.dk

🔗Nexus (website)

Matrix client made with Flutter and a Gomuks backend.

QuadRadical announces

🔗What's new?

Hello TWIM! Big news this week: Nexus v1.0.0 is out! 🎉 🎉 🎉 🎉 🎉 (and 1.0.1, oops :p)

The first stable release of Nexus, v1.0.0, just released! Unfortunately, it had a bug where power level settings would send invalid power level events, so I fixed this and released v1.0.1. You can grab it from the release page. If you use the Flatpak repo, the nightly builds, or the NixOS module, you're already set up, just update.

Since alpha1 last week, we released four more alphas before this stable. Thanks to everyone who tested them and reported bugs! Here's everything that changed along the way:

  • Room settings: You can now change a room's name, topic and other general settings, choose who can join (including knocking), and manage power levels, all from inside Nexus.
  • A profile editor, so you can change your own display name and avatar.
  • Typing indicators and read receipts.
  • Event search, to find messages in a room.
  • Knocking support, so you can ask to join rooms that use it.
  • Mutual rooms are now shown in user popovers.
  • Encryption setup: If your account doesn't have encryption set up yet, Nexus now walks you through it, instead of asking for a recovery key you don't have. If you've lost your recovery key, you can also reset your identity.
  • Downloading media: Save images, videos, audio, files and avatars to your device.
  • Swipe to reply on mobile (off by default, turn it on in settings!), and swipe in from the right to open the member list.
  • AVIF image support, including animated AVIFs.
  • Better notifications: On Android, messages from the same chat now stack into one conversation notification, with each sender's name and avatar. Group notifications on all platforms show who sent each message.
  • Nexus now uses your system's emoji, instead of bundling its own.
  • A new setting to hide membership events, thanks to @seres for contributing this!
  • A much smaller Android APK due to fixing a bug that caused multiple architectures of libmpv to get bundled, instead of just the relevant one.
  • And, as always, a whole lot of bug fixes 🙂

🔗What's next?

Krille - Christian K. announces

FluffyChat 2.11 is out (with two hotfix releases right after it). This release brings a lot of bugfixes and stability improvements under the hood and finally support for Windows and macOS.

🔗Try out our new desktop deployments

FluffyChat is now available as a beta on Windows and macOS. You can install the Windows version by downloading the installer from the GitHub release page:

For macOS you can join the open testflight group. Be aware that this is limited to 100 testers for now:

https://testflight.apple.com/join/Py6wnFGF

🔗Call improvements

Calls now also have audio on iOS, which was broken because of a bug in the audio session. LiveKit SFUs are also now discovered by the /rtc/transports endpoint from MSC4143.

A severe problem where the android app crashes regularly after closed with the back button has been fixed.

🔗Element X iOS (website)

A total rewrite of Element iOS using the Matrix Rust SDK underneath and targeting devices running iOS 17+.

Mauro says

Hi everyone! Here's what the Element X iOS team has been up to this week:

🔗✨ New and improved

  • Forward several messages at once: the multi-message forwarding we mentioned last time is done and now on for everyone. Pick a few messages and send them on together.
  • Missed calls while busy: if a call comes in while another one is ringing or already going, it now shows as a missed call instead of interrupting you.
  • See your recovery key as you type: the recovery key field now has a show/hide button.

🔗🚧 In progress

  • Multi-account support: each account now shares its live location separately, and we're doing the same for calls, so each call uses the account it was meant for.
  • Removing a device: you'll soon be able to check or set up your recovery key right from that screen.

🔗🐛 Fixes

  • "Create account" now opens the sign-up page, not the sign-in page.
  • Verifying a session from iOS with an Android device no longer leaves both devices waiting.
  • Live location shares now stop on time, even when the phone isn't moving.
  • Spatial photos sent in original quality now stay spatial.
  • Better accessibility: VoiceOver can find the settings button again, and the scroll buttons no longer get huge at larger text sizes.

🔗💜 Community

  • Thanks to rene-schakmann, who kept HDR photos in HDR when location data is removed, and stopped code from being hyphenated when it wraps in the timeline.
